text:
Josh Doan's first season in Buffalo told you he was more than Shane Doan's son: Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.2 wins above replacement in 2025-26, 42nd among 401 forwards, with his team creating noticeably more with him on the ice (97th percentile) and a habit of drawing more penalties than he takes. This season has been quieter. Four points in 17 games, three goals on 4.31 expected (the quality of his chances), and the Sabres losing the chance battle with him out there at five on five (46.5%).

Some of that is role. His ice time is down 1.6 minutes over his last ten games, to about 14.6 a night, and his points per 60 are well below the range our numbers think he's capable of. The tools are still loud: 92nd percentile top speed and 82nd percentile shot by NHL Edge. His last goal, against Columbus on Nov. 6, went in off him from a teammate's shot in tight, which is about how his luck has run. We'd expect the scoring to come back toward our projection of around 20 goals if Buffalo gives the minutes back.
